Ep. 441: A Small Word That Works Hard

This week we look at a small word that does a lot of work in spoken Hebrew. You hear it in the market, on the bus and in every argument between friends, and it rarely means what the dictionary says it means.

We start with how the word sounds when someone is surprised, then how it sounds when someone is tired of hearing the same excuse again. The difference is all in the melody, and we practise both.

Then we move to three expressions built around it. One is polite, one is friendly, and one you should probably keep for people who already know you well. We explain when each one fits and when it does not.

Along the way we meet a few verbs that like to travel with the word, and we notice how the stress moves when a suffix is added. If you have ever wondered why your teacher corrected you on this, now you know.

At the end of the episode there is a short dialogue between two neighbours who cannot agree about a parking spot. Listen to it twice: once for the meaning, and once only for the tone of voice.
